llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed local audit and policy helper for VMware skills, with sensitive audit-log handling that users should configure carefully.

dimensions.detail: It writes local state under ~/.vmware or OPS_HOME and checks only the presence of agent-identifying environment variables for audit attribution; this is proportionate, but the audit database may contain sensitive operational data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses a pinned uv package command for vmware-policy==1.20.0 and normal dependency use by related VMware skills; the artifact contains Markdown documentation only and no executable scripts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill is intentionally shared across the VMware skill family and auto-activates through the @vmware_tool decorator, which broadens impact but is clearly disclosed and aligned with the infrastructure role.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent local audit, rules, and undo databases are disclosed, permissioned best-effort, and purpose-aligned; no cron jobs, startup hooks, services, or hidden persistence were found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is coherent: it provides a Python decorator, local SQLite audit logging, optional policy rules, sanitization, and a CLI for VMware skill audit/policy workflows; it exposes no MCP tools itself.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want a shared local audit/policy layer for VMware skills. Treat ~/.vmware/audit.db and rotated archives as confidential, configure ~/.vmware/rules.yaml for production restrictions, avoid leaving VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 set, and make sure downstream VMware tools correctly declare sensitive parameters and sensitive results.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: The credential-related matches describe redaction controls and warnings for local audit rows, not evidence of credential theft or credential-store access; users still need to mark nonstandard secret fields as sensitive.
[SQP-1] expected: The shared auto-loaded role increases blast radius, but it is the core disclosed purpose of this policy/audit dependency.
[PE2] expected: The chmod commands are local file-permission hardening examples for ~/.vmware and audit.db, not sudo/root execution.
[RA2] expected: The persistent files are disclosed local audit/rules/undo state; no unauthorized cross-session execution mechanism was present.
[EA2] expected: The default policy baseline denying nothing is explicitly documented; this is an operator configuration caveat rather than hidden autonomous behavior.
[E3] expected: The filesystem command is a narrow troubleshooting check of ~/.vmware/rules.yaml, not broad enumeration or exfiltration.
